title: Client priority queue with conditional scope currency
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Build a transparent, negotiable "priority currency" that maps incoming high-touch customer requests into a bounded queue of roadmap slots. Each accepted request consumes a quantifiable amount of scope currency (e.g., engineering points + support runway + cross-functional coordination). The system enables PMs to: 1) objectively compare competing asks from strategic accounts, 2) communicate trade-offs to sales/CS, and 3) reserve runway with conditional commitments (partial deliveries, configurable SLAs).
background: Redwood receives frequent escalations from high-ARR and strategic accounts asking for roadmap acceleration or scope changes. Current intake is ad hoc: priority is sometimes decided in meetings, with inconsistent outcomes and little traceability. This causes negotiation friction with Sales/CS and creates unrealistic customer expectations. We need a repeatable mechanism that quantifies acceptance cost and provides fallback delivery patterns (partial rollouts, timeboxed engineering runway, discounted support add-ons).
goals: Create a scoring and currency model that translates account signals (ARR, renewal proximity, legal/contract risk, product fit) into a single priority index
Surface an immutable queue of accepted high-touch requests with attached ‘scope currency’ charge and delivery runway
Enable conditional commitments: partial features, staged rollouts, or alternative compensations (discounts, future credits) tied to currency refunds or retention clauses
Reduce negotiation time between PM/Sales/CS by 50% for high-touch intake and ensure operational traceability for executive review
success_metrics: Average decision time for a VIP intake reduced from 6 business days to <= 48 hours
% of accepted high-touch requests with explicit scope currency and delivery lane >= 90%
Renewal retention lift: measured cohort of accounts with accepted requests sees +4% net retention at next renewal
Number of post-commit scope disputes decreases by 70% as measured in support tickets and account reviews
scoring_model: Inputs: ARR, NPS, renewal date proximity, strategic signals (feature dependency), compliance/regulatory urgency, technical feasibility (eng estimate), and cross-org cost (SE/CS hours). Output: priority index 0-100 and a computed scope currency value (points + weeks of dedicated SE + QA hours). Currency is additive and consumable: each roadmap slot has a max currency budget and lower-priority requests can be charged partial refunds if a higher-priority item preempts the slot.
acceptance_criteria: UI: Intake form in Console for 'VIP Request' with fields required to compute the score
Backend: Automated scoring pipeline that returns priority index and scope currency within 1 minute of submission
Workflow: PM can accept/reject with a standard templated response; acceptance creates an immutable Queue item with metadata (score, currency, delivery lane, acceptance_date)
Negotiation: CS/Sales can propose compensations (credits, discounts, early access) that are recorded on the Queue item and billed to the currency ledger
Visibility: Executive dashboard showing queue positions, currency consumption, and projected impact to quarter OKRs
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (4 weeks): Prototype scoring engine and intake form; run shadow mode for incoming escalations; gather feedback from 6 pilot accounts and CS managers. Phase 2 (6 weeks): Enable PM acceptance and immutable queue; train Sales/CS; add templated negotiation responses and simple currency ledger. Phase 3 (ongoing): Attach delivery orchestration (canary/partial rollouts) and integrate with billing/discount workflows and legal approval flows.
risks: Overfitting to a small set of strategic accounts resulting in biased scoring
Perception risk: customers may view currency as a pay-to-play metric if not communicated thoughtfully
Operational overhead to keep currency ledger accurate across cross-functional teams
Legal/contract dependencies if compensations impact SLA or billing
notes: We should align this feature with the OKR: 'Improve enterprise booking predictability' and propose a dedicated 3% R&D runway for high-touch escalations for next quarter. Consider a 'currency refund' policy if we miss delivery SLOs for accepted items.
